sentences.text: Rule twenty-two is pure numbers: how far away each light must be visible.
I won’t pretend there’s a way around memorizing it, but there is a pattern.
Look at the table as it builds.
The masthead light is always the strongest.
Six miles on a vessel of fifty meters or more.
Five miles from twelve to fifty meters, but only three miles if she’s under twenty meters.
And two miles under twelve meters.
Sidelights: three miles, two miles, and one mile.
That one-mile sidelight on a small boat is the shortest range in the whole table.
The sternlight: three miles, two, and two.
The towing light matches the sternlight: three, two, and two.
And all-round lights are the same again: three, two, and two.
On a big ship, the masthead is six and everything else is three.
In the middle group, the masthead is five, or three under twenty meters, and everything else is two.
On a small boat, everything is two, except the sidelights, which are one.
